thread:
Maya (product): Quick sync — we need to lock priorities for the long-term platform roadmap section that affects routing policies + multi-region tenant isolation. Customer asks piling up, Q3 planning next week. What must be in scope vs can be deferred?
Liam (eng-runtime): Agree. Can we separate two streams: 1) customer-triggered hard requirements (security/residency/SLA), 2) foundational infra (routing policy engine, telemetry hooks).
Sasha (eng-platform): +1. From infra POV, building the routing policy engine is medium effort but blocks most of the canary/fallback work. Estimate: 4 wks core + 2 wks integrations.
Noah (architecture): Important callout: we should avoid a one-size isolation model. Propose 3 tiers: "soft fences" (logical routing rules), "hard lanes" (isolated pools w/ quotas), "airlock" (VPC/private deployments).
Claire (solutions): Customers A and B are asking for deterministic failover and region pinning for compliance. They need docs and a migration checklist, not just the engine.
Maya (product): Good framing. Priorities candidate list: a) routing policy DSL + simple UI, b) multi-region pinning + failover SLAs, c) tenant isolation lanes (hard lanes), d) migration playbook + docs. Which are M0 vs M1?
Liam (eng-runtime): M0: routing policy DSL + basic enforcement + telemetry. Without enforcement we can't guarantee isolation. M1: hard lanes + autoscale. M2: richer circuit-breakers and regional cost-aware routing.
Sasha (eng-platform): Add-on: KV-prefetch caching for pinned tenants — reduces tail latency in pinned region. That could be a small lift (1wk) but big perf win. Recommend include in M1 backlog.
Noah (architecture): Launch criteria suggestion for M0: 1) DSL deployed to canary orgs, 2) enforcement on 90% of routes, 3) SLI: 99th percentile routing decision time < 20ms, 4) documented rollback.
Claire (solutions): Also require customer-facing runbook + migration checklist as a gate for M1. Sales expects that before committing Dedicated deals.
Maya (product): Thanks. Let's capture owners and rough dates. Target: M0 start in 2 weeks, 6-week sprint. Owners: Liam (eng-runtime) lead, Sasha integration, Noah architecture review, Claire docs.
Liam (eng-runtime): I'll book a tech spec PR by EOD tomorrow. Quick note: capacity isolation needs a telemetry tag per request — we need an API change for token/profiles.
Sasha (eng-platform): If API change is small (header/tag), we can do a rollout without client changes by mapping existing tokens. But long-term we'll require client opt-in for stronger guarantees.
Noah (architecture): Risk: if we map tokens heuristically we can leak routing constraints. Need policy to default to conservative path. Add a security review.
Maya (product): Action items: 1) Liam spec + perf targets (owner: Liam) 2) Slack doc with isolation tiers & customer use-cases (owner: Noah + Claire) 3) Migration checklist draft (owner: Claire) 4) Eval plan & canary org list (owner: Sasha). Due: 3 business days.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy for feature/route-dsl-subsystem at 2024-07-18T02:00Z queued.
Claire (solutions): I'll pull in Customer A/B contacts to validate checklist.
Liam (eng-runtime): Noted. I'll flag any breaking API changes early.
Maya (product): Solid. If no objections I'll lock M0 on Fri and move these to the roadmap doc. Quick thumbs if you're aligned. :thumbsup:
